    How this wheel is built

    The chakra holds 1,989 events in chronological order, clockwise from the opening of the present kalpa to the foretold return of Satya Yuga, where the wheel closes on itself. Each ring carries one kind of event. Spacing is by sequence, not by years, so that crowded centuries stay readable.

    Three kinds of date are kept apart. Plain years are historically attested. Years marked “c.” are scholarly estimates, often with the range noted in the text. Dates marked “traditional” follow Purāṇic, Siddhāntic or sampradāya reckoning — Kali Yuga from 3102 BCE, or Ādi Śaṅkara at 788–820 CE — and are shown as the tradition gives them, with the scholarly view alongside where the two differ. Events of the Itihāsas and Purāṇas are placed by their traditional yuga, not asserted as dated history.

    Everything after 2026 is prophecy from the Bhāgavata, Viṣṇu, Brahmavaivarta and Kalki Purāṇas, or a scheduled observance, and is labelled so. Names follow IAST transliteration. “Background” notes explain recurring people, texts and places. Images load from Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons and link to their source pages for credit and licence.

    This is a living reference. If a date or attribution needs correcting, tell Tryambak Media and it will be fixed.
